identity.title: POCUS: anechoic dependent pleural collection with spine sign / lung flapping

technique.how: Curvilinear/phased-array (3.5-5 MHz) or higher-frequency probe at the posterior axillary line above the diaphragm, patient supine or sitting, indicator cephalad. Identify diaphragm, liver/spleen and an anechoic or hypoechoic dependent space between parietal and visceral pleura; look for the spine visible above the diaphragm (spine sign) and collapsed lung flapping within fluid.
technique.prerequisites: Basic thoracic POCUS training; adequate dependent window.

interpretation.positive_finding: Anechoic dependent collection with spine sign or lung flap is highly specific for pleural effusion (pooled specificity 0.98, LR+ ~54); echogenic or septated fluid suggests exudate/empyema/haemothorax.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of a dependent collection on a good window makes effusion unlikely (pooled sensitivity 0.94, LR- 0.06), far better than supine chest radiograph (sensitivity 0.51).
interpretation.pitfalls: Mirror artefact of liver above the diaphragm and subdiaphragmatic ascites can be mistaken for effusion; pocket-size devices and non-radiologist/intensivist operators had lower sensitivity. Effusion presence does not give the cause.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive scan confirms effusion and guides thoracentesis; negative scan should redirect the dyspnea work-up (HF without effusion, pneumonia, PE).

estimates.population: Mostly critically ill and trauma adults in ED/ICU; operators radiologist/intensivist (6 studies) or other physicians incl. emergency physicians (6)
estimates.reference_standard: Chest CT or surgery (studies using radiography as reference excluded)
estimates.quote: Pooled sensitivity and specificity of ultrasonography in detection of pleural effusion were 0.94 (95% CI: 0.88-0.97; I2= 84.23, p<0.001) and 0.98 (95% CI: 0.92-1.0;

estimates.target_condition: Pleural effusion - subgroup: operator 'other physician' (incl. emergency physicians), 6 studies
estimates.population: Adults, mostly critically ill/trauma, scanned by non-radiologist/non-intensivist physicians
estimates.reference_standard: Chest CT or surgery (studies using radiography as reference excluded)

estimates.target_condition: Pleural effusion - subgroup: radiologist or intensivist operator, 6 studies
estimates.population: Adults, mostly critically ill, scanned by radiologist/intensivist
estimates.reference_standard: Chest CT or surgery (studies using radiography as reference excluded)

estimates.target_condition: Pleural effusion - subgroup: pocket-size ultrasound device, 3 studies
estimates.reference_standard: Chest CT or surgery (studies using radiography as reference excluded)

sources.citation: Yousefifard M, Baikpour M, Ghelichkhani P, Asady H, Shahsavari Nia K, Moghadas Jafari A, Hosseini M, Safari S. Screening Performance Characteristic of Ultrasonography and Radiography in Detection of Pleural Effusion; a Meta-Analysis. Emerg (Tehran). 2016;4(1):1-10.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use to characterise effusion aetiology or to exclude small effusions when only anterior supine windows were obtained.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Large effusion with hypotension or respiratory distress, or echogenic fluid after trauma (haemothorax), needs urgent drainage/escalation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Not pooled; sensitivity differed by operator type (radiologist/intensivist 0.97 vs other physician 0.90, Table 2).
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Overall estimate mixes radiologists/intensivists and emergency physicians; use the 'other physician' subgroup (sens 0.90, spec 0.94) for a trained non-specialist POCUS user.

extraction_notes: Full text read via PMC. LR quote for overall estimate: 'pooled positive and negative likelihood ratios were calculated to be 53.96 (95% CI: 11.46-254.05; I2= 88.12, p<0.001) and 0.06 (95% CI: 0.03-0.12' (Results, Figure 4). Radiologist/intensivist subgroup sensitivity is printed as 0.97 (0.83-0.96) in Table 2 - the CI is internally inconsistent (likely a typo), so CI left null. Prevalence not pooled (mixed case-mix), left null. Reference standard: 'only surveys in which a final diagnosis of pleural effusion had been confirmed by computed tomography scan or surgery were included' (Methods). Comparator CXR pooled sens 0.51 (0.33-0.68), spec 0.91 (0.68-0.98) (Abstract). Spine sign / lung flap themselves were not separately evaluated; the pooled index test is ultrasonographic detection of effusion.
